title: Snorri Sturluson Icelandic Fellowships
description: An annual fellowship from the Government of Iceland, administered by the Arni Magnusson Institute for Icelandic Studies, granted to writers, translators, and scholars in the humanities (not to currently-enrolled university students) from outside Iceland. Fellows spend at least three months in Iceland to improve their knowledge of the Icelandic language, culture, and society, and are expected to produce a piece of writing, translation, or scholarly work connected to their stay. The award amount is based on travel expenses to and from Iceland plus a monthly living stipend; as of the most recently published figure (2019), the monthly stipend was approximately USD 1,245 (170,000 ISK) per fellow, though the exact amount fluctuates year to year based on the total funds allocated by the Icelandic state -- treat the USD figure as an approximate, dated reference point rather than a guaranteed current amount, since Icelandic krona isn't in this app's supported currency set and a precise up-to-date conversion wasn't available from the sources checked. When two equally qualified candidates are under consideration, preference is given to applicants from Eastern or Southern Europe, Asia, Africa, Latin America, or Oceania. Running annually since 1991, with applications due December 1 each year for the following year's fellowship. Cross-referenced across the Arni Magnusson Institute's own program description, the Government of Iceland's diplomatic-mission announcement, and UNESCO's Policy Monitoring Platform, all of which converge on the same eligibility, purpose, and December 1 deadline; the institute's own website was blocked from direct verification by this session's network restrictions.
org: Arni Magnusson Institute for Icelandic Studies (Government of Iceland)
visaNote: This is a short-term cultural/research fellowship, not employment; non-EEA fellows should confirm Iceland's long-stay visa/residence-permit requirements for a 3+ month stay well ahead of the start date.
